Precision.label: 02 · 2D drafting
Precision.title: Precise 2D drafting: object snaps, tracking and polar.
Precision.lead: Object snaps, tracking and polar angles behave the way your hands expect, and coordinates are typed the AutoCAD way, right at the cursor: @100<30 for relative polar, #120,80 for absolute.
Precision.osnapBody: {count, number} object snaps with AutoCAD's markers and tooltips. Shift+right-click forces one for the next pick — here, Tangent.
Precision.otrackBody: Rest on two points to acquire them, then follow their alignment paths to where they cross.
Precision.polarBody: Polar holds the rubber band to your increment and reads out distance and angle. Ortho locks it square.
Precision.selectionBody: Drag right for a window that takes what it encloses; drag left for a crossing that takes whatever it touches.
Precision.osnapAlt: A line being drawn to a circle, snapped to the tangent point, with the Tangent marker and tooltip.
Precision.otrackAlt: Two acquired endpoints and their dotted alignment paths crossing at the cursor.
Precision.polarAlt: A line locked to the 30 degree polar ray, with its distance and angle tooltip.
Precision.windowAlt: A blue window lasso dragged from left to right round a circle, across a line, with the circle it takes highlighted.
Precision.crossingAlt: A green, dashed crossing lasso dragged from right to left round a circle, across a line, with both highlighted.

LocalFirst.label: 04 · Free and private
LocalFirst.title: Free, with no sign-up and nothing to install.

Faq.label: 07 · FAQ
Faq.title: Questions, answered.
Faq.a1: Yes — free to use, with no account and no trial. It's an independent project under active development.
Faq.a2: Yes. The code is on <github>GitHub</github> under the MIT licence, and the engine is published on npm as <npm>{package}</npm>. The licence covers the code, not the MellowCAD name or logo.
Faq.q3: Do I need to install anything?
Faq.a3: No. It runs in a modern desktop browser — Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Open mellowcad.com/draw and type a command.
Faq.q4: Does it really work like AutoCAD?
Faq.a4: That's the spec: commands, aliases, prompt order, option letters and defaults follow current AutoCAD. Some commands are still partial, and the roadmap lists exactly which options are missing.
Faq.q5: Can I open or save DWG or DXF files, or print?
Faq.a5: Not yet. Drawings are saved in MellowCAD's own versioned file format, and there is no printing or PDF export yet. DXF import and export are on the roadmap but not scheduled yet.
Faq.a6: On your device. MellowCAD autosaves in your browser and never uploads your drawings. Clearing the site's data deletes the autosave, so press Ctrl+S to keep a file.
Faq.a7: No. It's an independent project. AutoCAD is a registered trademark of Autodesk, Inc.
Faq.q8: Does it work on tablets or phones?
Faq.a8: It opens, but it's built for a keyboard and mouse, like AutoCAD. Use a computer.
Faq.a9: {commands, number} commands, including LINE, PLINE, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, HATCH, OFFSET, TRIM, FILLET, ARRAY, dimensions, blocks and layers. The <reference>command reference</reference> lists every one, with its aliases and first prompt.
Faq.a10: In part. It builds 3D solids — primitives, extrusions and revolutions, unions, subtractions and intersections, slices and sections, filleted and chamfered edges, edited faces — measures their mass properties, and shows them in orbit, from the ViewCube and in shaded visual styles. Sweeps, lofts, meshes and rendering are not there yet.
Faq.q11: Can I use it to practise for my AutoCAD class?
Faq.a11: Yes, for the commands: their names and aliases, the order of their prompts and their options follow AutoCAD, in English, Spanish or Brazilian Portuguese. It cannot open or save DWG files yet, so work you hand in as DWG or PDF still needs another program.

Privacy.metaDescription: What MellowCAD keeps in your browser, what it measures, who handles that data and on what grounds, and your rights.
Privacy.label: Privacy
Privacy.title: What stays where.
Privacy.lead: MellowCAD has no accounts and no servers that see your drawings. This is everything it keeps, everything it measures, and who handles it.
Privacy.stored1: Your drawing, autosaved in the browser's local storage as you work. It never leaves the device.
Privacy.stored2: Nothing else, and no cookies. The live sketch on the home page keeps its drawing in the page's memory and forgets it when you leave.
Privacy.storedNote: Clearing this site's data in your browser deletes the autosave. Press Ctrl+S in the editor to keep a file.
Privacy.analytics1: Vercel Web Analytics counts page views: the page, the page you came from, your country and city, and your browser, system and type of device. It sets no cookies; a visit is recognised by a hash of the request, discarded after 24 hours, and the statistics are anonymous.
Privacy.analytics2: Vercel Speed Insights reports how fast pages load and respond, with the page, your browser, system, type of device, network speed and country — anonymously too.
Privacy.analytics3: Neither sees your drawings, and neither is used for advertising, profiling or any automated decision.
Privacy.handled1: MellowCAD is an independent project by {name}, who is responsible for this data and answers at <email>{address}</email>.
Privacy.handled2: Serving the site and measuring its use and speed rest on a legitimate interest in running a free service well, kept to anonymous statistics (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Privacy.handled3: Vercel Inc. hosts the site and runs both measurements. Like any host, it processes your IP address to deliver the pages. It is based in the United States and certified under the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
Privacy.handled4: If you write, your message is handled by Google, the email provider, and used only to answer you, for as long as the conversation needs.
Privacy.rights1: You can ask to access, correct or delete data about you, to restrict or object to its use, or to receive a copy of it: write to the address above.
Privacy.rights2: You can also complain to a data protection authority — in the EU, the one where you live or work.

Docs.pages.exercises.title: AutoCAD practice exercises
Docs.pages.exercises.metaTitle: AutoCAD practice exercises, free, with solutions
Docs.pages.exercises.description: AutoCAD practice drawings for beginners and up, in 2D, isometric and 3D, each solved step by step and opened with its drawing in a free online editor.
Docs.pages.exercises.lead: Drawings to practise AutoCAD on, from a first gasket to 3D solids, each with its dimensions, the commands it practises and its solution step by step. The engine draws every step and writes its command-line history as you will type it: the prompts in AutoCAD 2027's order, with the same option letters. Open one in the editor and its drawing is there beside the space where you draw yours, in your browser, with nothing to install and no account to make.
Docs.pages.exercises.guides: The exercises' skills one at a time: typing points, a house's floor plan, a 2D drawing turned into a solid. Each guide shows every step's drawing and its history.
Docs.pages.exercises.how: An exercise opens in the editor with its drawing, dimensioned, left of the origin: draw yours from 0,0, as its solution does. What you draw is kept in this browser for that exercise alone. The drawing you were working on stays as it was, and the editor opened on its own brings it back. To start an exercise again, run NEW, then open it from its page. Every page prints on its own, the drawing first and the steps after, and your browser's print dialog saves it as a PDF.
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.where.que: Where can I find AutoCAD exercises to practise?
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.where.ans: Here: each exercise has its drawing dimensioned, the commands it practises and its solution step by step, and opens in a free editor that works like AutoCAD, in the browser. Start with the beginner ones; each command they use leads to what it does and the options it asks for.
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.online.qu: Can I practise AutoCAD online for free?
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.online.an: Yes. MellowCAD runs in the browser, free and with no account: you type AutoCAD's commands and aliases, in your language's names, and answer their prompts in the same order, with the same option letters. It is not AutoCAD: it does not open DWG or DXF files yet, and its 3D solids are still partial.
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.solutions: Every exercise is solved step by step under its drawing. The engine draws each step and writes the command line's history, so you can compare yours with it line by line.
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.pdf.quest: Can I print the exercises or save them as a PDF?
Docs.pages.exercises.questions.pdf.answe: Yes. An exercise's page prints on its own, dark lines on white, the drawing first and the steps after, and your browser's print dialog saves it as a PDF.

Docs.exercise.stepsLead: The engine draws each step and writes its history as you would type it: the prompts in AutoCAD 2027's order, with the same option letters. After a command's first point, a typed point is measured from the last one, as dynamic input measures it, and the history writes it with @; # measures from the origin.
